extracted.intended_audience: Readers of epd medien; media professionals and anyone interested in press ethics and media accountability in Germany
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing journalistic content against the German Presserat / Pressekodex to determine breaches warranting Rügen (reprimands). Covers standards such as verification/diligence, protection of personal rights, separation of advertising, and application of press-ethical rules to AI-generated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistische Sorgfaltspflicht (duty of care)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‚journalistische Sorgfaltspflicht‘ — the duty of journalistic care and verification; the Presserat cited this most frequently (43 cases) as the reason for Rügen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure facts are checked and verified before publication; do not publish unverified assertions as established facts; use reliable sourcing and corroboration. Failure to verify may lead to a Rüge (example given where reporting repeated an army claim without proof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persönlichkeitsschutz (protection of personal rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‚Verletzungen des Persönlichkeitsschutzes‘ — protection of individuals' personal rights and honor; the Presserat issued Rügen for breaches (30 cases) such as naming victims without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing identifying information about victims without consent; respect privacy and personal dignity; refrain from reporting that unduly harms a person's reputation or personal sphere. Naming crime victims or making damaging allegations without consent/evidence constitutes a breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gebot der Trennung von Werbung und Redaktion (separation of advertising and editorial)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‚Gebot der Trennung von Werbung und Redaktion‘ — the requirement to keep advertising and editorial content clearly separated; 21 Rügen were issued for violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear and visible distinction between paid/promotional material and independent editorial content; avoid blending advertorials with journalism or presenting ads as news. Proper labelling and structural separation are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Pressekodex to AI-generated content / editorial responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presserat's position: ‚Alle pressethischen Regeln gelten auch im Umgang mit KI‘ and those who commit to the Pressekodex ‚trage die presseethische Verantwortung für alle redaktionellen Beiträge. Das gelte unabhängig von der Art und Weise der Erstellung auch für künstlich generierte Inhalte.‘
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers and editors remain fully responsible for press-ethical compliance of content regardless of whether it was human- or AI-created. Existing press-ethical rules apply; the Presserat did not see a need (at time of report) for a separate AI-labeling obligation, but ethical obligations (accuracy, protection of rights, separation of advertising, etc.) must be enforced for AI outputs as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines must not state unverified allegations as facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines that assert allegations without evidence violate the Presserat's standards (example: a headline stating someone was 'Anführer einer Zelle der Terrororganisation Hamas' without proof was judged a breach of Sorgfaltspflicht and a grave violation of personal honour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure headline wording is supported by confirmed facts and evidence; avoid sensational or definitive language about culpability or organizational leadership unless substantiated. Headlines should not elevate unproven claims into factual statements that can damage reputations.
